commands.name: semantic-batch
commands.description: Processes batches of items (documents, images, data rows) using semantic understanding. Use when asked to classify, extract, filter, or summarize many items at once - like "process these 50 CVs into a spreadsheet" or "categorize these 1000 product descriptions". Handles text, images, PDFs, Excel, and mixed inputs. (user)

commands.name: arch-retrieval
commands.description: Retrieval checklist for answering questions from the Arch API. Use when working with portfolio holdings, tasks, activities, cash flows, tax documents, or Arch-linked files. Emphasizes orientation before extraction, exact evidence for claims, and avoiding unsupported historical assertions. (user)

commands.name: dev-browser
commands.description: Browser automation with persistent page state. Use when users ask to navigate websites, fill forms, take screenshots, extract web data, test web apps, or automate browser workflows. Trigger phrases include "go to [url]", "click on", "fill out the form", "take a screenshot", "scrape", "automate", "test the website", "log into", or any browser interaction request. (user)

commands.name: seer
commands.description: (sentry) Ask natural language questions about your Sentry environment and get detailed insights using the Sentry MCP server

commands.name: getIssues
commands.description: (sentry) Fetch the most recent 10 issues from Sentry, optionally filtered by project name

commands.name: codex:adversarial-review
commands.description: (codex) Run a Codex review that challenges the implementation approach and design choices

commands.name: codex:result
commands.description: (codex) Show the stored final output for a finished Codex job in this repository

commands.name: codex:setup
commands.description: (codex) Check whether the local Codex CLI is ready and optionally toggle the stop-time review gate

commands.name: codex:status
commands.description: (codex) Show active and recent Codex jobs for this repository, including review-gate status

commands.name: codex:cancel
commands.description: (codex) Cancel an active background Codex job in this repository

commands.name: codex:rescue
commands.description: (codex) Delegate investigation, an explicit fix request, or follow-up rescue work to the Codex rescue subagent
commands.argumentHint: [--background|--wait] [--resume|--fresh] [--model <model|spark>] [--effort <none|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh>] [what Codex should investigate, solve, or continue]

commands.name: codex:review
commands.description: (codex) Run a Codex code review against local git state

commands.name: sentry-code-review
commands.description: (sentry) Analyze and resolve Sentry comments on GitHub Pull Requests. Use this when asked to review or fix issues identified by Sentry in PR comments. Can review specific PRs by number or automatically find recent PRs with Sentry feedback.

commands.name: sentry-setup-ai-monitoring
commands.description: (sentry) Setup Sentry AI Agent Monitoring in any project. Use this when asked to add AI monitoring, track LLM calls, monitor AI agents, or instrument OpenAI/Anthropic/Vercel AI/LangChain/Google GenAI. Automatically detects installed AI SDKs and configures the appropriate Sentry integration.

commands.name: sentry-setup-tracing
commands.description: (sentry) Setup Sentry Tracing (Performance Monitoring) in any project. Use this when asked to add performance monitoring, enable tracing, track transactions/spans, or instrument application performance. Supports JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Ruby, React, Next.js, and Node.js.

commands.name: sentry-setup-logging
commands.description: (sentry) Setup Sentry Logging in any project. Use this when asked to add Sentry logs, enable structured logging, setup console log capture, or integrate logging with Sentry. Supports JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Ruby, React, Next.js, and other frameworks.

commands.name: sentry-setup-metrics
commands.description: (sentry) Setup Sentry Metrics in any project. Use this when asked to add Sentry metrics, track custom metrics, setup counters/gauges/distributions, or instrument application performance metrics. Supports JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, React, Next.js, and Node.js.

commands.name: access
commands.description: (telegram) Manage Telegram channel access — approve pairings, edit allowlists, set DM/group policy. Use when the user asks to pair, approve someone, check who's allowed, or change policy for the Telegram channel.

commands.name: configure
commands.description: (telegram) Set up the Telegram channel — save the bot token and review access policy. Use when the user pastes a Telegram bot token, asks to configure Telegram, asks "how do I set this up" or "who can reach me," or wants to check channel status.

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff for correctness bugs at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill — a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

commands.name: clear
commands.description: Start a new session with empty context; previous session stays on disk (resumable with /resume)

commands.name: compact
commands.description: Free up context by summarizing the conversation so far

commands.name: context
commands.description: Show current context usage

commands.name: heapdump
commands.description: Dump the JS heap to ~/Desktop

commands.name: init
commands.description: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation

commands.name: review
commands.description: Review a pull request

commands.name: security-review
commands.description: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

commands.name: usage
commands.description: Show the total cost and duration of the current session

commands.name: insights
commands.description: Generate a report analyzing your Claude Code sessions

commands.name: goal
commands.description: Set a goal — keep working until the condition is met

commands.name: team-onboarding
commands.description: Help teammates ramp on Claude Code with a guide from your usage

agents.name: claude
agents.description: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed.

agents.name: code-simplifier
agents.description: Simplifies recently modified code for clarity and maintainability while preserving exact functionality.

agents.name: codex:codex-rescue
agents.description: Proactively use when Claude Code is stuck, wants a second implementation or diagnosis pass, needs a deeper root-cause investigation, or should hand a substantial coding task to Codex through the shared runtime

agents.name: Explore
agents.description: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions.

agents.name: general-purpose
agents.description: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you.

agents.name: Plan
agents.description: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs.

agents.name: sentry:issue-summarizer
agents.description: Analyze multiple Sentry issues in parallel to provide comprehensive summaries of user impact, root causes, and patterns. Use this when you need to understand the overall health of a project or investigate multiple related issues.

agents.name: statusline-setup
agents.description: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting.

Haiku 4.5 · Fastest for quick answers · $1/$5 per Mtok
